newsitem.title: USA: Clinton pledges action to cut U.S. pollution.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pledges action to cut U.S. pollution.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, pledging that the United States will do more to control its own greenhouse gases, on Thursday pledged $1 billion in aid to developing countries help them cut their emissions.

"To help developing nations reduce greenhouse gas emissions, I am pleased to announce that the U.S. will provide them with $1 billion in assistance over the next five years," Clinton said in remarks prepared for delivery at the U.N. Earth Summit.

"These funds will go to programmes that support energy efficiency, develop alternative energy sources and improve resource management to promote growth that does not adversely affect the climate," Clinton said.

Sensitive to the complaints of European leaders that the United States has failed to commit itself to clear reductions in carbon dioxide emissions, Clinton said he would seek specific targets when a U.N. conference on global warming meets in Kyoto, Japan at the end of the year.

"We will work with our people -- and we will bring to the Kyoto conference in December a strong American commitment to realistic and binding limits that will significantly reduce our emissions of greenhouse gases," Clinton said.
"Here in the United States, we must do better," Clinton said, noting that "with 4 percent of the world's population, we produce 20 percent of its greenhouse gases."
"So we must do better, and we will," he said, saying "This is a challenge we must undertake immediately and one in which I personally plan to play a critical role."
